claims.text: Equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloys such as WMoTaNb can possess a single-phase BCC structure.
Conventionally cast or SPS-processed equiatomic BCC refractory alloys have relatively coarse grains.
Conventionally processed equiatomic BCC refractory alloys contain few twin boundaries.
An optimized low-temperature anneal, optionally combined with mild thermomechanical processing, can produce nano-twins in the BCC matrix.
The proposed treatment can refine the BCC matrix to an ultrafine grain structure.
The treatment-induced nano-twinned, ultrafine-grained microstructure will remain stable during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting twin boundaries will be coherent and present at high density.
Nano-twins impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Refined grain boundaries impede elevated-temperature creep deformation.
Twin-boundary and grain-boundary strengthening will increase high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance.
Refractory HEAs, including BCC WMoTaNb, can retain substantial strength at temperatures above 1000°C.
The proposed annealing benefit should hold above 1000°C under compression or creep loading.
The treated alloy should show approximately 20–30% higher high-temperature yield strength than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy should have a lower high-temperature creep rate than the untreated alloy.
The treatment should preserve room-temperature ductility and toughness.
The processing intervention should not increase density because it does not add heavy secondary phases.
Excessive annealing temperature or time can cause grain growth that negates the strengthening benefit.
Excessive annealing can precipitate secondary dense phases and degrade high-temperature or room-temperature properties.
